items.aboutTitle: A sacred dip, offered in your name
items.aboutText1: Punya Snan is the holy bath taken in a sacred river on an auspicious day. It is believed to cleanse the mind, remove past sins and bring the blessings of the river goddess to the devotee and their family.
items.aboutText2: Many devotees cannot travel to Haridwar, Prayagraj or Varanasi because of distance, health or work. With Virtual Punya Snan, our priests take the sacred dip on your behalf with your name, gotra and photograph, following the full Vedic process.

items.jaapIntroText:
Mahamrityunjay Jaap is the sacred chanting of the Mahamrityunjay Mantra from the Rigveda, dedicated to Lord Shiva in his form as the conqueror of death. Performed in sets of 108, 1,008, or 1,25,000 repetitions, this jaap is believed to invoke Lord Shiva's grace for health, long life, protection, and liberation from the cycle of birth and death.

Our experienced priests perform the jaap on your behalf with a proper sankalp in your name and gotra, following Vedic procedures. You receive a recorded video and prasad.
items.jaapMantra:
ॐ त्र्यम्बकं यजामहे
सुगन्धिं पुष्टिवर्धनम्।
उर्वारुकमिव बन्धनान्
मृत्योर्मुक्षीय माऽमृतात्॥
items.jaapMeaning: We worship the three-eyed Lord Shiva, who is fragrant and nourishes all beings. May He free us from the bondage of death, just as a ripened cucumber is freed from its vine, and grant us liberation.
items.jaapCol1Text: The Mahamrityunjay Mantra addresses Lord Shiva as the three-eyed one who perceives past, present and future. Chanting it with devotion is believed to create a protective shield around the devotee.
items.jaapCol2Text: This jaap is performed for the recovery of serious illness, protection from untimely death, relief from grief and fear, and to seek Lord Shiva's blessings for a long and healthy life.
items.jaapCol3Text: The Mahamrityunjay Mantra appears in the Rigveda (7.59.12) and is one of the most powerful Vedic mantras. It is chanted in temples, hospitals, and homes to invoke divine protection and spiritual healing.

items.jaapIntroText:
Sundarkand is the fifth chapter of the Ramcharitmanas composed by Goswami Tulsidas and also of the Valmiki Ramayana. It narrates the journey of Lord Hanuman to Lanka to find Mata Sita, and is considered the most sacred and powerful chapter of the Ramayana. Its recitation is believed to bring courage, peace, success, and relief from difficulties.

Our priests recite the complete Sundarkand Path on your behalf with a sankalp in your name, following traditional procedures.

जय हनुमान ज्ञान गुन सागर।

items.jaapMeaning: Victory to Hanuman, the ocean of wisdom and virtue. Victory to the Lord of monkeys, who illuminates the three worlds.
items.jaapCol1Text: Sundarkand describes Lord Hanuman's flight to Lanka, his search for Mata Sita, his encounter with Ravana, and his return with news that brings hope to Lord Rama. It is the chapter of courage and devotion.
items.jaapCol2Text: The path is performed for the removal of obstacles, courage in difficult times, success in important endeavours, peace in the home, and to invoke Lord Hanuman's protection over the family.
items.jaapCol3Text: Sundarkand is considered so auspicious that its regular recitation is believed to ward off evil, remove fear, and bring the blessings of both Lord Rama and Lord Hanuman to the devotee's household.

items.jaapIntroText:
Durga Saptashati, also known as Devi Mahatmyam or Chandi Path, is a sacred text of 700 verses from the Markandeya Purana that describes the victory of Goddess Durga over the demon forces. It is one of the most important texts of Shakti worship and is recited during Navratri and other occasions dedicated to the Divine Mother.

Our priests recite the complete Durga Saptashati with a sankalp in your name, following traditional procedures with all thirteen chapters.
items.jaapMantra:

items.jaapMeaning: Salutations to the Goddess who resides in all beings in the form of Shakti (divine power). We bow to Her, again and again.
items.jaapCol1Text: The Durga Saptashati consists of 700 shlokas in 13 chapters describing three episodes of Goddess Durga's victory over demonic forces — Madhu-Kaitabh, Mahishasura, and Shumbha-Nishumbha.
items.jaapCol2Text: It is performed to seek Goddess Durga's blessings for protection, strength, removal of obstacles, success, and victory over adversity. It is especially recited for the well-being of the family during difficult times.
items.jaapCol3Text: The Durga Saptashati is one of the most sacred texts in the Shakta tradition. Its recitation during Navratri is considered especially powerful. Every verse is believed to carry the energy of the Divine Mother.

The Hanuman Chalisa is a devotional hymn of forty verses composed by Goswami Tulsidas in praise of Lord Hanuman. It is one of the most widely recited prayers in the Hindu tradition and is believed to invoke Lord Hanuman's protection, courage, and blessings. Its daily or special recitation is a part of millions of Hindu households.

Our priests recite the Hanuman Chalisa on your behalf in multiples of 108, 1,008, or more, with a sankalp in your name and full devotion.

items.jaapMeaning: Having cleansed the mirror of my mind with the dust of the Guru's lotus feet, I recite the pure glory of Shri Raghuvira, which bestows the four fruits of life.
items.jaapCol1Text: The Hanuman Chalisa is a forty-verse prayer composed by Tulsidas in the 16th century. It describes Lord Hanuman's divine qualities, his devotion to Lord Rama, and his role as a protector and remover of fear.
items.jaapCol2Text: It is recited for courage, protection from negative forces, relief from fear and anxiety, success in difficult tasks, and to seek Lord Hanuman's blessings for the family's well-being.
items.jaapCol3Text: The Hanuman Chalisa is believed to be especially powerful when recited on Tuesdays and Saturdays. Continuous recitation — 108 times or more — is considered an act of deep devotion to Lord Hanuman.

items.jaapIntroText:
Rudrabhishek is the sacred ritual of bathing the Shivalinga with panchamrit — milk, curd, honey, ghee, and sugar — while chanting the Rudrashtadhyayi or the Laghu Rudra from the Krishna Yajurveda. It is one of the most important forms of Lord Shiva's worship and is believed to bring immense divine grace, health, and prosperity.

Our priests perform Rudrabhishek on your behalf with a proper sankalp in your name, using pure and auspicious ingredients according to Vedic tradition.

नमः शम्भवाय च मयोभवाय च
नमः शङ्कराय च मयस्कराय च
नमः शिवाय च शिवतराय च॥
items.jaapMeaning: Salutations to Lord Shiva who is the source of joy, the giver of bliss, the auspicious one, the bestower of happiness, the Shiva and the supremely auspicious.
items.jaapCol1Text: Rudrabhishek is the ritual bathing of the Shivalinga with sacred substances — milk, curd, honey, ghee, sugar, water from holy rivers — while reciting the Rudrashtadhyayi, invoking Lord Shiva in his Rudra form.
items.jaapCol2Text: Rudrabhishek is performed for health, long life, protection of the family, removal of planetary afflictions, success in business and education, and to seek Lord Shiva's blessings in all areas of life.
items.jaapCol3Text: The Rudri recited during Rudrabhishek comes from the Krishna Yajurveda and is considered one of the most powerful Vedic texts. Each recitation of the Rudrashtadhyayi is equivalent to Laghu Rudra, and eleven such recitations constitute the Maharudra.

The Gayatri Mantra is the most sacred mantra of the Vedic tradition, appearing in the Rigveda (3.62.10). Known as the mother of the Vedas, it is addressed to Savitar — the divine sun — and invokes divine intelligence to illuminate the mind. The Navarna Mantra — ॐ ऐं ह्रीं क्लीं चामुण्डायै विच्चे — is the nine-syllable (nava-akshara) mantra of Goddess Chamunda Durga. items.jaapCol3Text: The Navarna Mantra is the heart of the Durga Saptashati and is recited at the beginning and end of the path. It combines the energies of the three primary goddesses — knowledge, wealth, and power — into a single mantra.
